exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Solana (SOL) traded at $96.7800 as of 2026-11-05 08:40:52 UTC, -0.35% over one hour and +3.77% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $92.4600 to $97.8600; spot sits at 80% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink SOL/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $95.0978, 13.8 hours before the spot quote and -1.74% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price sits at $96.78, comfortably within the upper‑80% of the 24‑hour range ([Ex. B]), indicating buyers have already captured most of the intraday upside and are likely to sustain the current level through the next 24 hours.  

2. Despite a seven‑day decline of 4.20% ([Ex. C]), the 24‑hour average ($95.09) exceeds the 72‑hour average ($93.50) and the RSI remains neutral at 59.6 ([Ex. D]), showing short‑term buying pressure is outweighing the longer‑term downtrend.  

3. Liquidity is ample with $4.07 billion traded in the past day ([Ex. E]), and the Chainlink feed, the settlement benchmark, lags the spot by only 1.74% ([Ex. G]), ensuring execution at a price firmly above the feed and thus a clear long edge.  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price sits near the upper 80% of its 24‑hour range [Ex. B], yet the seven‑day average remains below the current level ($95.09 vs. $93.50) indicating a short‑term rebound that is likely to cap and reverse as traders take profits [Ex. C].  

2. Realized volatility is modest at 3.15% per day [Ex. D] while the RSI at 59.6 signals a market that is edging toward over‑extension; a modest pullback should therefore be swift and measurable.  

3. Liquidity is ample ($4.07 bn, 7.13% of market cap) [Ex. E] and the neutral Fear & Greed Index [Ex. F] suggests no defensive buying pressure, allowing a short position to be entered and closed cleanly at the Chainlink settlement price of $95.0978 [Ex. G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point collapses under Exhibit B: the price sits at 80 % of the 24‑hour range, but that range is narrow ($92.46‑$97.86) and still expanding upward, contradicting any “capped” rebound. Moreover, Exhibit C shows the 24‑hour average ($95.09) already exceeds the 72‑hour average ($93.50), evidencing upward momentum, not a peak ready to flip.  

The second point misreads momentum: Exhibit D’s RSI of 59.6 is well within the neutral band (30‑70), and the modest 3.15 % daily volatility signals a market capable of sustaining gains, not an imminent pull‑back.  

Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s first premise collapses on the range metric: at 80% of the 24‑hour span the price sits near the top, but the upper bound is only $97.86, a mere $1.08 ceiling that leaves negligible upside and signals exhaustion rather than durability [Ex. B]. The second premise ignores the prevailing seven‑day decline and the modest volatility of only 3.15% per day, which together imply limited upside momentum; a neutral RSI of 59.6 does not constitute “short‑term buying pressure” but merely a balance point [Ex. C, D]. Hence the evidence forecloses a sustainable rise and undermines the Bull’s case. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds the evidence insufficient to justify a practice position.

findings.finding: Spot price is $96.78, up 3.77% in 24h but down 0.35% in the last hour.
Current price sits at 80% of the 24‑hour range, indicating limited upside room.
Seven‑day trend is –4.20%, with price below the 7‑day high and above the 7‑day low.
Realized volatility is modest (3.15%/day) and RSI is neutral at 59.6.
Fear & Greed Index reads 50, indicating neutral market sentiment.

ruling.opinion: The Court notes that while the 24‑hour gain and spot level suggest some short‑term strength, the price occupies the upper 80% of a narrow range, the seven‑day decline signals broader bearish pressure, and both volatility and sentiment remain neutral. No exhibit provides a decisive edge for either side, leading to a dismissal of a practice position.
ruling.dissent: The Bear argues that the limited upside within the 24‑hour range and the prevailing seven‑day downtrend outweigh the modest short‑term gains, warranting a short position.

sentence.reason: The case was dismissed; no practice position is ordered.
